repositories.name: metadata-graph
repositories.reason: Owns the column model, graph store, metadata REST API and the metadata.dataset.changed.v1 event; must store a per-column classification, suggest it from ingested source tags, expose a steward override endpoint and include classification in column responses and change events.

repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Spec of record for the metadata-graph OpenAPI and the event schemas (metadata.dataset.changed.v1, ingestion.schema.discovered.v1), so the additive fields, the new classification endpoint and the access-decision masked_columns field must be defined here first.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: MetadataClient is the mandated REST client for metadata-graph and the events helper wraps publish/subscribe, so it needs the classification field on column models and a set-classification method for stewards and the DQ service.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Produces ingestion.schema.discovered.v1, whose column payload today carries only name/type/nullable, so it must parse source column comments/tags (e.g. 'tags: pii,email') and emit them as an optional tags field.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and makes access decisions, so it must retain column classifications and return the list of columns to mask when the requester lacks a pii:read grant.

repositories.name: reporting-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and is the only known service returning data to consumers, so it must apply the masked_columns from the access decision to query/report results (and must be re-verified against the additive event fields).

repositories.name: dq-service
repositories.reason: Publishes dq.result.published.v1 and runs data-quality checks, so it must look up column classifications (via platform-sdk MetadataClient) and apply PII-format validation rules to columns classified PII.

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lowercase strings parsed from the source column comment/tags, e.g. ['pii','email']); absent means no tags.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional dataset.columns[].classification (PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII) and columns[].classification_source (SUGGESTED|STEWARD); classification changes are published with the existing change_type COLUMNS_CHANGED rather than a new enum value.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Each column object gains classification and classification_source fields; existing fields unchanged.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: Steward-only endpoint to set or override a column classification (body {classification, reason?}); returns the updated column, 400 on invalid value, 404 on unknown dataset/column, 403 without steward role, and publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1.

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decisions
contracts.description: Access decision response gains masked_columns (list of column names classified PII that must be masked because the requester lacks pii:read); empty list when nothing must be masked.

open_questions: What are the exact repository names of the ingestion service and the data-quality service (assumed ingestion-service and dq-service)?
Is reporting-service the component that returns query results to data consumers, or is there a separate query gateway/engine repository that must apply masking?
What is the exact path and shape of the entitlements access-decision API (assumed POST /v1/access/decisions)?
What classification should unclassified/legacy columns default to (null vs INTERNAL), and should masking fail closed for unclassified columns?
Should CONFIDENTIAL columns also be masked for some requesters, or only PII columns lacking pii:read?
What is the tag-to-classification mapping (e.g. pii/email/phone/ssn -> PII, confidential -> CONFIDENTIAL, public -> PUBLIC, otherwise no suggestion)?
Which masking format is required (full redaction, partial e.g. a***@x.com, or hash/tokenisation), and must masked results stay type-compatible?
Do metadata.dataset.changed.v1 consumers validate change_type against a closed enum (which would make a new CLASSIFICATION_CHANGED value breaking)?
Which identity/role provides the steward permission for the override endpoint, and is an audit trail of overrides required?
Which PII-format rules does the DQ service need (email, phone, SSN, ...) and how should a PII column be mapped to a rule (by tag subtype or by classification only)?
Do dq.result.published.v1 results need a per-rule breakdown for the PII checks, which would change that event contract?
